title: you're not the only one
hookLine: you're not the only one; the room at sunset
tomorrow: look at something bigger than you today

lines: A FULL ROOM, AND STILL ALONE.
cards: You can feel it in a full room. At a party where everyone seems to know everyone. In a group chat that's buzzing with jokes you're not part of.
At 2am, awake, when the whole building seems to be asleep but you. Loneliness is strange that way. It isn't about how many people are near you.
It's the feeling that nobody is really with you. And one of its cruelest tricks is convincing you that you're the only one who feels it. You're not.

teach.h: HALF OF ADULTS SAID THEY'D FELT IT.
teach.b: In 2023, the Surgeon General of the United States issued a formal public health advisory about loneliness, the kind usually saved for things like smoking.
It reported that about half of American adults said they'd experienced it. Half. Which means that in almost any room, a good number of the people are quietly feeling what you feel.

The old texts knew this ache. Near the start of the Bible, before anything has gone wrong in the garden, God looks at the first human and says, in the King James wording: "It is not good that the man should be alone."

teach.h: THE FIRST THING CALLED NOT GOOD.
teach.b: It's the first thing in the whole story called not good. Old prayers are full of people saying so, out loud: turn to me, for I am alone.
The night before he dies, Jesus asks his closest friends to stay awake with him while he prays, and they fall asleep.

teach.h: ALONE ISN'T THE SAME AS LONELY.
teach.b: Many traditions have noticed that being alone and being lonely aren't the same thing. The same hour on your own can feel like a punishment or like a rest. Monks and hermits choose solitude.
Now, the room at sunset. At this hour, somewhere, a family is lighting candles. Someone is unrolling a prayer mat.
Someone in a monastery is singing the evening prayers, someone is sitting on a cushion, someone is just stopping on a balcony to watch the light. You can't see them. They can't see you.
But you're all doing the same small, brave thing at the same kind of hour. The room is full.

how: Many traditions meet loneliness with shared practice at set hours, so that people praying or sitting alone know others are doing the same, and with care for those on their own, such as visiting the sick and the isolated.

games.q: the night before he dies, Jesus asks his closest friends to stay awake with him while he prays. what do they do?
o: stay awake and pray with him.
games.why: they fall asleep. even at the center of the Gospel story, someone knows what it is to be alone among friends.

practice: Here's the practice. Sit, and let the breath settle. For about seventy-five seconds, picture the room at sunset.
Somewhere, someone lighting a candle. Someone kneeling. Someone sitting just like you, a little tired, stopping anyway.
You don't know their names. On each breath out, let yourself be one of them. If loneliness is heavy today, let it be here too.

wordCard.voice: Loneliness. The feeling that nobody is with you, and one of the most widely shared feelings there is. Eighteenth word.

carryVoice: Your line: the room is full. And if the loneliness is heavy today, telling one person is a brave and good first step. Day eighteen.
